prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim. Injury: concussion. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1396; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a report of a low-speed collision in a parking lot. Claimant reports being struck by a vehicle while stopped in a marked space. Claimant states they were checked at the scene and transported to urgent care. Injury reported as concussion with headache and dizziness. Claimant is not represented by counsel. Photos of both vehicles requested.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. Claimant describes ongoing headaches and sensitivity to light since the incident. Claimant has not yet received a medical diagnosis summary and asked how the claim process works. Explained the general steps for injury and property damage coverage. Requested copies of urgent care discharge paperwork and any follow-up referrals.

Entry 3: Received police report from the parking lot incident. Report notes both drivers were stationary or moving at low speed and no citations were issued. Other driver's insurer has been identified and contacted to confirm liability position. Awaiting their response before making a determination on fault.

Entry 4: Claimant emailed the urgent care records and a note from a primary care provider recommending rest and a follow-up in two weeks. Reviewed the medical documentation for consistency with the reported injury. Claimant mentioned missing several days of work and asked whether lost wages could be included. Advised that wage loss documentation from the employer will be needed to evaluate that element.

Entry 5: Followed up with claimant regarding outstanding documents. Claimant confirmed the follow-up appointment is scheduled and has agreed to provide an employer wage statement. Vehicle inspection completed and repair estimate received. Claim remains open pending medical follow-up, wage documentation, and the other insurer's liability response. Reminded claimant they may consult an attorney at any time if they wish.
